summary: Mrinal Kaul is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned degrees from St. Stephen's College, University of Delhi, University of Oxford, and Concordia University, and held positions at Concordia, University of Naples "L'Orientale", Manipal Academy, and IIT Bombay.

Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as a Professor at Vidyasagar College (attested 1970–1975) and taught in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982, 1994).

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He has held positions at Leipzig, Heidelberg, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Muhamad Saputra is a PhD student at the Australian National University, studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron (attested 2026).

Muhamed Riyaz Chenganakkattil is an Indologist and historian who studied at Darul Huda Islamic University, Jamia Millia Islamia, and IIT Delhi (PhD 2016–2024). In 2024, he held fellowships at IIT Delhi and Ghent University.

Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as Deputy Director at the Taxila Museum, Director at the Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).

Muhammad Nasim Khan is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who earned an M.Phil from the University of Peshawar. His career includes posts at Peshawar, the University of Hamburg, and the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Muhammad Shahidullah (1885–1969) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi. He held key posts at the University of Dhaka, University of Rajshahi, and Bangla Academy.

Muhammed Niyas Ashraf is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin (2015–2024) and held a postdoctoral fellowship at Ghent University (2025–2026).

Mukesh Mehta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at Banaras Hindu University (2019–2022) and was a Research Associate at the International School for Jain Studies in 2023.

Mukund Lalji Wadekar is an Indologist who served as Officiating Director at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 2002–2008) and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 2008), as well as General Editor for Gaekwad's Oriental Series.
Mukund Ram Shastri (d. 1921) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who served as Head Pandit at the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1911 and 1916–1918).

Mukunda Raj Aryal works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Apex College and Tribhuvan University, where he served as a professor (attested 2003); he also served as Head at Apex College in 2017.

Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Hanazono University and under Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot of Shofuku-ji, president of Hanazono University (1949–1978), and head of the Institute for Zen Studies.

Mun-keat Choong is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Queensland under Roderick S. Bucknell. From 2003 to 2025, he served as Lecturer in Studies in Religion at the University of New England.

Munenobu Sakurai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his doctoral course at Tohoku University. He served as an assistant professor at Iwate University (1994–2005) and later as a professor at Tohoku University.

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and earned his PhD from Harvard University. He held faculty posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology and Kyoto University, where he was appointed Professor in 1990.

Muneyoshi Yanagi (1889–1961) was a Japanese scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He was educated at the University of Tokyo between 1910 and 1913 and studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki.

Mungunchimeg Batmunkh is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who completed a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Brigitte Marschall (attested 2010).

Munis D. Faruqui is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an Associate Professor at the University of California, Berkeley, and became Director and Sarah Kailath Chair at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.
